guide.summary: Use OpenProject's documented authorization-code OAuth flow with a confidential application and the api_v3 scope. Register the application on a representative test instance, authorize a test user, then test read-only GET /api/v3/work_packages with offset and pageSize. Provider review, customer-instance approval rules, the exact work-package visibility permission and the title field name are not established by the supplied sources. Writes and deletes are excluded.

findings.title: Register a confidential OAuth application on the target instance
findings.detail: An administrator creates the OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications, with a redirect URL, the Confidential option, and a noted Client ID and secret.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Check if the application will be Confidential . This is typically the case for client applications running on a server or desktop but requires the client application to ensure it.
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

findings.title: Request the api_v3 scope for standard API access
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is assumed when no scope is checked. It is the scope this read uses.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Avoid unrequested scopes
findings.detail: No narrower read-only scope is documented in the supplied sources. Do not request bcf_v2_1, which is specific to the BIM edition, or scim_v2, which this read does not need.

evidence.quote: standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.
<scope> with list of scope values separated with %20 . e.g. scim_v2%20api_v3

findings.title: Use authorization-code consent for each connected person
findings.detail: Each customer user authorizes through the authorization URL with prompt=consent, and the code is exchanged for a bearer token. Client credentials acts as a configured user, so it does not fit per-person access.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
Typically the server that was requested with that redirect will save the authorization code and use it to obtain API token, with which the server can then act on behalf
(Optional) Choose Client Credentials User and define a user on whose behalf requests will be performed.

findings.title: Use offset, pageSize and an empty filters array
findings.detail: offset is a page number and pageSize sets results per page. Send filters as an empty array so no default filter is applied.

evidence.quote: Page number inside the requested collection.
Number of elements to display per page.
optional query JSON specifying filter conditions. Accepts the same format as returned by the queries endpoint. If no filter is to be applied, the client should send an empty array

steps.title: Register a confidential OAuth application on a test instance
steps.detail: Create the application on a test OpenProject instance with the api_v3 scope and Confidential checked. Record the Client ID and Client secret for later use.
steps.doneWhen: The application appears in the OAuth applications list with a Client ID and secret recorded.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Check if the application will be Confidential . This is typically the case for client applications running on a server or desktop but requires the client application to ensure it.
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

steps.appliesWhen: Only if you have administrator access to a test OpenProject instance

steps.title: Implement the callback and code-to-token exchange
steps.detail: Build the callback that receives the authorization code and exchanges it at the token endpoint. The instance host is supplied by the user.
steps.doneWhen: The callback code is ready and reviewed, and no token has been requested yet.

steps.title: Authorize a test user and exchange the code for a token
steps.detail: Sign in as the representative test user and approve consent. The exchange returns an access token and refresh token with scope api_v3.
steps.doneWhen: The token response includes an access_token, a refresh_token and scope api_v3.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.
"scope" : "api_v3" ,

steps.title: Test read of the first page of work package titles
steps.detail: Send a read-only GET to list work packages. Record the titles of the returned work packages and confirm the response is a collection.
steps.doneWhen: The response is a work package collection and at least one title is recorded from the first page.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
pageSize integer optional query
optional query JSON specifying filter conditions. Accepts the same format as returned by the queries endpoint. If no filter is to be applied, the client should send an empty array

fields: instance-host (customer instance base URL, user input)

steps.title: Test pagination by requesting a later page
steps.detail: Repeat the GET with offset=2 and compare the titles with the first page to confirm pagination returns different results.
steps.doneWhen: The second page returns a collection and its titles differ from the first page.

evidence.quote: Parameters offset integer optional query
Page number inside the requested collection.
Number of elements to display per page.

fields: instance-host (customer instance base URL, user input)

steps.detail: Confirm the test client issues no POST, PATCH or DELETE calls to work package endpoints. The listing endpoint is documented as a collection read.
steps.doneWhen: The test log or client code shows only GET requests to work package endpoints.

evidence.quote: get /api/v3/work_packages Returns a collection of work packages.
